tags: why does my dog look away from me
script: You call out to your dog, and instead of looking at you, they turn their head away. It's easy to take that personally, but in dog language, looking away is usually a polite, calming gesture, not rudeness. Dogs use head turns, lip licks and soft blinks as calming signals to defuse tension and show they mean no harm. If you've just scolded them, leaned over them, or stared intensely, a head turn can mean they're feeling a little uneasy and are trying to ease the situation. Direct stares can feel confrontational to dogs, so averting their eyes helps keep things friendly. It can also happen when they're overwhelmed, tired, or distracted by something more interesting, like a smell. And sometimes a dog simply hasn't understood the cue, which is a training gap, not defiance. To help, soften your body language, use a calm voice, crouch down to their level and reward them whenever they do check in with you. That teaches them that looking at you is safe and rewarding. If your dog avoids eye contact only with specific people or situations, notice the pattern, because it tells you what makes them nervous.
